```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
options(digits=2)
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
require(lubridate)
kRdata <- read.csv(file = 'kRdata.csv')
kRdata <- kRdata %>%
mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
kData = kRdata
```
Data are from the Patient_Info dataset from South Korea 1 Jan to 1 May 2020. These data were retrieved from a downloadable zip file from kaggle.

Some of the data were uncoded for sex - sex must be just male or female.  77 of the data entries were coded sex as blank, so we omit these.  State of a patient must be died or alive - we adjust that as well.  This is done in the mutate function. 

Variables of interest: sex, result

Research Question: - Is dying independent of sex?

# Introduction

Using the Kdata, are we able to determine if men and women are equally likely to die of covid19 from data collected in south korea through May 2019. 

$H_A$  There is a realtionsjop between gender and death of Covid-19 in Korea.  

$H_0$  There is no relationship between gender and death from Covid-19 in Korea.
